procedure.description: inpatient admission, septicemia or severe sepsis without mechanical ventilation over 96 hours, with major complication or comorbidity

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for MS-DRG 871 (inpatient admission, septicemia or severe sepsis without mechanical ventilation over 96 hours, with major complication or comorbidity) with dates of service 2026-02-04 through 2026-02-08. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: Inpatient level of care is not supported by the clinical documentation. Observation services were appropriate for the services rendered; the claim is denied as billed.

criteria.text: Sepsis documented by a suspected or confirmed infection with at least two systemic inflammatory response criteria or a qSOFA score of 2 or more, together with evidence of hypoperfusion or organ dysfunction such as a lactate of 2 or more or hypotension.
Treatment required inpatient-level resources: intravenous fluid resuscitation of 30 mL/kg, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, serial lactate measurement, and continuous hemodynamic monitoring.

At the time of the admission order, the admitting physician documented a reasonable expectation that care would span at least two midnights, and the actual stay met that expectation or was shortened by an unforeseen event.
The condition could not be safely treated with outpatient or observation services.

chart.text: 76 year old woman brought in by her daughter with two days of fever, chills, and left-sided back pain, poor oral intake since yesterday. History of hypertension and chronic kidney disease. On arrival temperature 39.2, heart rate 118, respiratory rate 24, blood pressure 86 over 50, oxygen saturation 94 percent on room air. Looks sick. Left flank tenderness, urine cloudy. Working diagnosis pyelonephritis with sepsis.

Admission history and physical. Assessment: pyelonephritis. Plan as above. Family updated at the bedside. 2.25 liters of lactated Ringer’s given as a 30 per kilo bolus in the department, piperacillin-tazobactam started within the hour. Repeat lactate every 6 hours until cleared, telemetry, strict intake and output, hold the lisinopril. Admit inpatient. I expect this admission to span at least two midnights: she needs 48 hours of intravenous antibiotics pending cultures, lactate clearance, and recovery of renal function before any oral step-down is safe.
Lactate 4.1. White count 16.1 with 12 percent bands. Creatinine 1.8, baseline 1.0 from last year. Urinalysis: many white cells, nitrite positive. Blood and urine cultures sent.
Daily weight 196 pounds, up 0 from yesterday. Intake and output recorded. Repositioned per schedule, skin checked.
Bowel regimen started, senna and docusate at bedtime. Last bowel movement 3 days ago per patient. Encouraged fluids and ambulation as able.
Fall risk assessment completed, score 54, high risk. Bed alarm on, nonskid socks, call light within reach, hourly rounding. Family at bedside this evening.
Potassium 3.1 this morning, repleted with 20 milliequivalents oral per protocol. Recheck with morning labs.
Overnight: vital signs every 2 hours, two episodes of rigors, warm blankets, acetaminophen given. Tolerating sips. Urine output recorded hourly.
Hospital day 2 labs. Lactate 2.1 at 12 hours. White count 15.0. Creatinine 1.9. Blood cultures: gram-negative rods in 2 of 2 bottles, identification pending.

Hospital day 2. Not an observation candidate: blood pressure dipped to 84 over 48 overnight requiring a third liter, lactate 2.6 at 6 hours and 2.1 at 12 hours, creatinine 1.9 this morning. Continue intravenous antibiotics and fluids, nephrology aware.
Pneumococcal vaccine status reviewed, up to date per state registry. Influenza vaccine offered and accepted, given left deltoid.
Pharmacy note. Renal dosing reviewed, creatinine 0.8, no adjustments needed today. Home medication list reconciled with the daughter by phone, one duplicate statin removed.

Hospital day 3. Improving. Temperature maximum 37.9, heart rate 92, blood pressure 108 over 66 without fluids since this morning. Lactate 1.6. Creatinine 1.5. Cultures pending speciation. Advance diet, continue intravenous antibiotics.
Day 3 nursing. Ambulated in the hall with standby assistance twice, tolerating a regular diet, voiding without difficulty, pain 2 out of 10. Intravenous antibiotics infusing on schedule.
Dietitian consult. Regular diet with no added salt modification. Intake about 60 percent of meals. Supplement shake twice daily added. Will follow.
IV site rotated from the left forearm to the right hand, old site without redness. Dressing dated. Patient tolerated well.
Audiology screen at nursing's request. She wears a hearing aid on the right, battery replaced, hears conversational voice well now. No further needs.
Home levothyroxine resumed at the home dose this morning after review with the attending. No interactions flagged.
Social work met with the patient and her son to confirm the home address, the primary contact, and transportation for follow-up appointments. No barriers identified today.
Hospital day 4. Afebrile 36 hours, lactate 1.1, creatinine back to 1.1, cultures grew E. coli sensitive to cefpodoxime. Discharged home on oral antibiotics.
Skin assessment on admission. Braden 17. Skin intact, no pressure injury, heels floated. Turn every two hours while in bed. Barrier cream to the sacrum as a precaution.
Chaplain visited at the patient's request, about twenty minutes. She appreciated the visit. No needs identified.
Dentures labeled and placed in the denture cup at the bedside. Patient prefers them out at night. Oral care done.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
